content: Live birth refers to the process in which an embryo develops inside the mother’s body, as opposed to being laid as an egg. For more information on this biological process, refer to the concept of vivipary. A live birth is defined as the event in which a fetus, regardless of its gestational age, exits the maternal body and subsequently exhibits any sign of life. These signs of life may include voluntary movement, a detectable heartbeat, or pulsation of the umbilical cord. This definition applies even if these signs are present for only a brief period and irrespective of whether the umbilical cord or placenta remains intact. The term live birth was formally defined by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 1950. This definition is primarily used for public health and statistical purposes. It is important to note that the mode of delivery, whether vaginal or via Caesarean section, and the ultimate viability of the neonate are not factors considered in this statistical definition. However, the term live birth was in common usage long before its formal definition in 1950. In the United States, the term born alive is specifically defined under federal statute.
